# Equipment Service Desk

**AI-generated demonstration. This synthetic PHP/Symfony project was generated by a coding agent without my supervision during its original development. It is not a client project, has no production deployment or real users, and is not presented as evidence of personally supervised implementation.**

This repository contains a fictional equipment-request workflow. The source, tests, and commands below describe that artifact; this page does not certify it as an authoritative reference design. Later documentation or automated checks do not change its original development provenance.

## The demonstration workflow

Register equipment → submit a request → confirm triage → assign a technician → record resolution → inspect history and download an asynchronous report.

The synthetic implementation describes requester, technician, and coordinator roles; policy snapshots; idempotency records; optimistic assignment versions; a PostgreSQL-backed report queue; and bounded report output. These are characteristics of this codebase, not a claim that a real organization used it.

## Run locally

Requirements: Docker Engine with Compose v2 or newer, Git, Make, and Python. Containers supply PHP and Composer. Make passes the current Linux UID/GID to bind-mounted development services; see [operations](docs/operations.md) for direct Compose use.

```sh
make init
make install
make db-up
make migrate
make fixtures
make up
make token ACTOR=coordinator-a
```

The API listens only on `http://127.0.0.1:8089`. Token issuance writes an ignored, owner-only curl configuration file and prints only its relative filename and token ID. Use the reported file with `curl --config <reported-file>`; do not paste tokens into commands, logs, or source.

`.env.example` documents the variables. `make init` generates `.env.local` without overwriting existing configuration; Compose and Symfony then load it. The database has no host port. The demonstration contacts no real equipment service.

## Try the documented workflow

```sh
make walkthrough
make check
```

The walkthrough is documented to create its own disposable database and loopback-only HTTP stack. It exercises the fictional request flow, replay, cross-user denial, stale assignment, a worker, and CSV download, then removes only its own containers and temporary token files.

`make check` is the project's local acceptance command. Its documented gates cover unit and PostgreSQL integration tests, API/OpenAPI contracts, concurrency and worker behavior, migrations, static analysis, formatting, configuration, documentation, dependency review, privacy scanning, the walkthrough, and a production-image smoke check. See [testing](docs/testing.md) for scope and evidence limits. These commands describe the repository's checks; a check result applies only to the specific source state where it was run.

## Deliberate limits

The fictional scope is one organization with three roles. It has no frontend, uploads, email, external identity provider, inventory integration, or configurable rules language. Reports are bounded to 31 days, 10,000 rows, and 5 MiB. Reports and idempotency records have no automatic retention policy.

Audit history is application-level, not tamper-proof. Queue delivery is at least once, not exactly once. A nonlocal deployment requires TLS and a separately reviewed configuration. The project has no production deployment, real users, or measured-scale claim, and is not presented as a personal reference implementation.
